GENERAL SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Plant Growth and Development 1.7 Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reaction? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Plant Growth and Development 1.7 Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reaction.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Plant Growth and Development 1.7 Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reaction.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Plant Growth and Development 1.7 Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reaction.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Plant Growth and Development 1.7 Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reaction.

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemical Families ● Alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases ? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemical Families ● Alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Chemical Families ● Alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases .
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemical Families ● Alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases .
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemical Families ● Alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases .

5. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Microorganisms ● Types of microorganisms ● Mode of transmission and infections o? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Microorganisms ● Types of microorganisms ● Mode of transmission and infections o.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Microorganisms ● Types of microorganisms ● Mode of transmission and infections o.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Microorganisms ● Types of microorganisms ● Mode of transmission and infections o.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Microorganisms ● Types of microorganisms ● Mode of transmission and infections o.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transport in plants ● Absorption of Water and Mineral Salts ● Translocation ● Fa? (1 mark)

   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transport in plants ● Absorption of Water and Mineral Salts ● Translocation ● Fa.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reactions 2.1 The Periodic Table 2.2 Chem? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reactions 2.1 The Periodic Table 2.2 Chem.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reactions 2.1 The Periodic Table 2.2 Chem.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reactions 2.1 The Periodic Table 2.2 Chem.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Microorganisms 2.0 Matter and Chemical Reactions 2.1 The Periodic Table 2.2 Chem.

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Respiration ● Aerobic and anaerobic respiration ● Respiratory substrates and res? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Respiration ● Aerobic and anaerobic respiration ● Respiratory substrates and res.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Respiration ● Aerobic and anaerobic respiration ● Respiratory substrates and res.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Respiration ● Aerobic and anaerobic respiration ● Respiratory substrates and res.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Respiration ● Aerobic and anaerobic respiration ● Respiratory substrates and res.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Periodic Table 2.2 Chemical Families 2.3 Chemical Bonding 2.4 Acids, Bases a? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Periodic Table 2.2 Chemical Families 2.3 Chemical Bonding 2.4 Acids, Bases a.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Periodic Table 2.2 Chemical Families 2.3 Chemical Bonding 2.4 Acids, Bases a.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Periodic Table 2.2 Chemical Families 2.3 Chemical Bonding 2.4 Acids, Bases a.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Periodic Table 2.2 Chemical Families 2.3 Chemical Bonding 2.4 Acids, Bases a.

   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Periodic Table Classification of the first twenty elements of the periodic t.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Periodic Table Classification of the first twenty elements of the periodic t.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in Animals ● Chemical and mechanical digestion of foods ● Adaptations ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in Animals ● Chemical and mechanical digestion of foods ● Adaptations .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in Animals ● Chemical and mechanical digestion of foods ● Adaptations .
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in Animals ● Chemical and mechanical digestion of foods ● Adaptations .
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in Animals ● Chemical and mechanical digestion of foods ● Adaptations .

15. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

16. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. A mixture of two liquids

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Magnetism and electromagnetic induction ● Magnetisation and demagnetisation ● Ma and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to General Science ● Importance of General Science, ● Careers in Ge and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain The Cell ● Types of microscopes ● Differences between light and electron microsc and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in Animals ● Chemical and mechanical digestion of foods ● Adaptations  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Transport in plants ● Absorption of Water and Mineral Salts ● Translocation ● Fa and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Respiration ● Aerobic and anaerobic respiration ● Respiratory substrates and res and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
